ROI-Inspector is a Python desktop application (Tkinter GUI) designed to compare specific regions between a reference document/object (image or PDF) and a real image, which can come either from a live camera capture (OpenCV) or from an image file provided by the user.
It supports OCR text comparison, shape/contour comparison, and includes a 4-point geometric alignment step to ensure accurate matching.

1. Core Functionality
A. Load a Reference

Load a reference image (PNG/JPG/BMP) or a PDF page (via PyMuPDF).

Display it on a Tkinter Canvas with zoom/pan.

User draws multiple ROIs (Regions of Interest).

ROIs can be edited, named, deleted, and saved to JSON (normalized coordinates).

B. 4-Point Alignment (Geometric Calibration)

Before comparison, the user defines four corresponding points on both the reference image and the real image to enable perspective and scale correction.

1. On the Reference

User selects 4 keypoints (corners, markers, or chosen reference points).

Stored consistently (e.g., clockwise order).

2. On the Real Image

The real image can come from:

a live camera feed, OR

a user-selected image file.

User selects the same four points in corresponding positions.

3. Alignment Step

Compute a homography matrix via cv2.findHomography.

Warp the real image to align it with the reference (cv2.warpPerspective).

This step corrects:

perspective

rotation

scale

slight camera angle deviations

It dramatically improves OCR and contour matching accuracy.

C. Real Image Input (Two Options)
1. Capture From Camera

Live preview using OpenCV (VideoCapture).

“Capture Image” button saves the frame.

User selects 4 alignment points afterward.

2. Import User Image

User can load an external image file instead of using a camera.

Shown side-by-side with the reference.

User selects 4 alignment points.

Both input methods follow the same processing pipeline after alignment.

2. ROI Comparison Modes

Each ROI can be assigned one of the modes below.

A. OCR Comparison (Text Mode)

In each aligned ROI:

Preprocess (threshold, denoise, deskew).

Run OCR engine:

Tesseract (pytesseract), or

EasyOCR / PaddleOCR for enhanced robustness.

Clean up extracted text.

Compare with reference ROI text using:

Levenshtein distance

fuzzy matching

difflib ratio

Output:

extracted text

similarity percentage

highlighted differences

B. Shape / Contour Comparison (Object Mode)

In each ROI:

Extract edges and contours.

Compare with reference using:

cv2.matchShapes()

keypoint matching (ORB/SIFT + RANSAC)

Output:

contour similarity score

pass/fail

optionally, highlight mismatched areas

3. Export & Reporting

Save complete project (reference, ROIs, alignment points).

Export comparison results in JSON.

Annotated output images:

aligned real image

ROI comparisons

difference highlights

4. Technical Stack

Tkinter for GUI

OpenCV for camera access, alignment, contour detection

PyMuPDF for PDF handling

Pillow (PIL) for image display

Tesseract / EasyOCR / PaddleOCR for OCR

numpy for math

python-Levenshtein / difflib for text comparison

5. Processing Pipeline (Full Workflow)

Load reference image or PDF page.

Draw one or more ROIs.

Select 4 alignment points on the reference.

Provide the real image:

capture from camera, or

load image file.

Select the same 4 alignment points on the real image.

Compute homography and warp the real image.

For each ROI, extract both aligned regions.

Apply OCR or contour comparison.

Present similarity results with visualization.

Export results (JSON + annotated images)."

please continue, also use this stackoverflow reply for help your self:I see steps are scattered in different answers. Based on my recent experience with this pytesseract error on Windows, writing different steps in sequence to make it easier to resolve the error:

1. Install tesseract using windows installer available at: https://github.com/UB-Mannheim/tesseract/wiki

2. Note the tesseract path from the installation. Default installation path at the time of this edit was: C:\Users\USER\AppData\Local\Tesseract-OCR. It may change so please check the installation path.

3. pip install pytesseract

4. Set the tesseract path in the script before calling image_to_string:

pytesseract.pytesseract.tesseract_cmd = r'C:\Users\USER\AppData\Local\Tesseract-OCR\tesseract.exe'
